note.p: This is a one-sided relationship - Bain is always the venue. This probably because he is related to Godwin's business concerns, and that suggests that this might well be William Bain, who was the Captain of a The City of Edinburgh, a packet ship that ploughed its way between London and Leith, and which may have been crucial for the sending of books to Murray in Edinburgh. A young artist, named Bain, who executed a medallion from Chantry's bust of Sir Walter Scott, is mentioned in the Morning Chronicle for March 12, 1823, which is praised for preserving the resemblance, being executed in the best possible taste and distinguished for its breadth and simplicity. There is also a Joseph Bain, printer of A Few Words respecting the Probability of a Revelation of the Nature and Will of the Deity (1824). But we think William Bain is the more likely recipient of Godwin's regular calls in this period!
